name: Thai-Inspired Peach and Lentil Salad With Lemongrass Dressing

ingredients.name: French green lentils, picked over and rinsed
kosher salt, plus more to taste
ripe but firm medium peaches, pitted and cut into wedges
loosely packed fresh mint leaves, roughly chopped
loosely packed fresh Thai leaves, roughly torn
loosely packed fresh cilantro leaves, tender stems roughly chopped

instructions.primary_message: For the Dressing: In a blender, combine lemongrass, ginger, garlic, chile, lime juice, rice vinegar, fish sauce, palm sugar, and olive oil. Blend on high speed until sugar has dissolved and dressing is smooth, scraping down sides of blender as needed, about 1 minute. Set aside.

For the Salad: In a medium saucepan, cover lentils with cold water by about 2 inches. Add salt and bring to a boil over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to maintain a gentle simmer and cook until lentils are tender but still hold their shape, 15 to 18 minutes. Drain well.

Transfer warm, drained lentils to a large bowl. Add 3/4 cup reserved dressing and toss thoroughly to coat. Let stand for 15 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, to allow lentils to absorb dressing. Set remaining dressing aside.

Add peaches, mint, basil, cilantro, and fried shallots and toss gently to combine. Taste lentils and add more dressing to taste, reserving any remaining dressing for another use. Season to taste with salt.
For Serving: Transfer salad to a serving platter. Sprinkle sliced chiles, mint, basil, and fried shallots over top. Serve.

description: This Thai–cuisine–inspired make-ahead summer salad pairs juicy peaches and tender lentils with fresh herbs, fried shallots, and a punchy lemongrass-lime dressing.
notes:
Optional substitutions: red pepper → green chile pepper; palm sugar → light brown sugar; loosely packed fresh Thai leaves → sweet basil leaves; red chile peppers → green chile peppers; Thai basil leaves → sweet basil leaves

Notes: Any variety of fresh green or red chile, such as serrano, Fresno, or Thai bird chile, will work in this recipe. Adjust the quantity to taste, taking into account the varying heat levels of different chile varieties.

Make-ahead and storage: The dressing can be made up to 4 days in advance and refrigerated in an airtight container.
Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Laila Ibrahim
